text:
Acme Mutual Home Claims Guide
Sample document. Acme Mutual Insurance Company is a fictional company created for this demonstration.

Reporting a claim
Report a loss as soon as possible, ideally within 72 hours. You must report a claim no later than 60 days after the date of loss, or Acme may deny it. You can report a claim in the Acme app, online at acme.example/claims, or by phone at the fictional claims number 1-800-555-0142, which is open 24 hours a day.

When you report a claim you receive a claim number. Keep it handy, because every message about the claim uses it.

What to do right after a loss
First make sure everyone is safe. Then take reasonable steps to prevent more damage, for example covering a broken window or shutting off the water. Acme reimburses reasonable emergency repairs up to 2,500 dollars without prior approval, so keep every receipt. Do not throw away damaged items until the adjuster has seen them or told you that photos are enough.

If your home cannot be lived in, keep receipts for hotel stays, meals and other extra costs so they can be paid under Coverage D.
section: What to do right after a loss

text:
Documents you will need
Take photos or videos of all damage before you clean up. Make a list of damaged or stolen items with their approximate age and value. For a theft, you must file a police report within 48 hours of discovering the theft and give Acme the report number.

The adjuster visit
Acme assigns an adjuster within 2 business days after you report a claim. The adjuster contacts you to schedule an inspection, which usually takes place within 7 days. For small claims under 5,000 dollars, Acme may settle the claim from photos without an inspection, through the Fast Track process.

How claims are paid
Acme makes a coverage decision within 30 days after it receives your signed proof of loss. Once you and Acme agree on the amount, payment is sent within 10 business days by direct deposit or check. Payments for a mortgaged home include your mortgage company as a payee.

For dwelling losses settled at replacement cost, Acme first pays the actual cash value. The remaining amount, called recoverable depreciation, is paid once repairs are completed, as long as they are completed within 180 days of the first payment.

Disagreeing with a decision
If you disagree with the amount of a loss, you can ask for appraisal in writing within 60 days of the claim decision. You and Acme each choose an independent appraiser, and the two appraisers choose an umpire. A written agreement by any two of the three sets the amount of the loss. You pay your own appraiser, and the umpire's cost is shared equally.

Acme Mutual Home Insurance Policy (Form AH-3)
Sample document. Acme Mutual Insurance Company is a fictional company created for this demonstration. Nothing in this document describes a real insurance product.
section: Acme Mutual Home Insurance Policy (Form AH-3)

text:
About this policy
This policy is a contract between you, the named insured shown in the Declarations, and Acme Mutual Insurance Company. The policy period is twelve months and starts at 12:01 a.m. on the effective date shown in the Declarations. The policy renews automatically for another twelve months unless you or Acme decide not to renew it. Acme will mail a renewal offer at least 45 days before the policy period ends. The policy is made up of the Declarations page, this policy form, and any endorsements you have chosen. If an endorsement conflicts with this form, the endorsement applies.

Coverage A: Dwelling and Coverage B: Other Structures
Coverage A pays to repair or rebuild your house, including attached structures such as an attached garage, deck or porch. Losses to the dwelling are settled at replacement cost, which means the cost to repair or replace with materials of like kind and quality, without a deduction for depreciation, once the repair is actually completed. The most Acme pays is the Coverage A limit shown in the Declarations. Coverage B pays for structures on your property that are not attached to the house, such as a detached garage, a fence or a garden shed. The Coverage B limit is 10 percent of the Coverage A limit. Structures used for business purposes are not covered under Coverage B.
section: Coverage A: Dwelling and Coverage B: Other Structures

text:
Coverage C: Personal Property and Coverage D: Loss of Use
Coverage C pays for personal property you own or use anywhere in the world, such as furniture, clothing and electronics. The Coverage C limit is 50 percent of the Coverage A limit. Personal property is settled at actual cash value unless you buy the Replacement Cost Contents endorsement HE-07. Special limits apply to some types of property for any one loss: cash and gift cards up to 200 dollars, theft of jewelry and watches up to 1,500 dollars, theft of firearms up to 2,500 dollars, and business property kept at home up to 2,500 dollars. Coverage D pays additional living expenses, such as hotel bills and extra meal costs, when a covered loss makes your home unfit to live in. The Coverage D limit is 20 percent of the Coverage A limit, and Acme pays these expenses for the shortest time needed to repair the home, up to a maximum of 12 months.
section: Coverage C: Personal Property and Coverage D: Loss of Use

text:
Exclusions
Acme does not pay for loss caused by any of the following: flood, surface water or waves; earthquake or earth movement; wear and tear, rust or gradual deterioration; damage by insects, rodents or birds; intentional loss caused by an insured person; and war or nuclear hazard. Water that backs up through sewers or drains is excluded unless you add the Water Backup endorsement HE-12, which provides up to 10,000 dollars per loss. Mold is excluded, except that Acme pays up to 5,000 dollars for mold removal when the mold results from a covered water loss.

Deductibles
A deductible is the amount of each covered loss that you pay before Acme pays. The standard all-peril deductible is 1,000 dollars. You may choose a 500 dollar or a 2,500 dollar deductible instead, which changes your premium. Losses caused by windstorm or hail have a separate deductible equal to 2 percent of the Coverage A limit. The deductible applies once per occurrence, even if more than one coverage part is involved in the same loss.

Premium Payments and Cancellation
You can pay the premium annually, in two semi-annual payments, or in monthly installments. Each monthly installment carries a 3 dollar service fee. If a payment is late, there is a grace period of 15 days before Acme sends a notice of cancellation. You may cancel this policy at any time by contacting Acme. If you cancel, Acme refunds any unearned premium on a pro rata basis, with no cancellation fee. If Acme cancels for nonpayment of premium, it will give you at least 10 days written notice. If Acme cancels for any other allowed reason, it will give at least 30 days notice. After the policy has been in force for 60 days, Acme may cancel only for nonpayment, fraud, or a substantial change in the risk.

Discounts
The following discounts may reduce your premium. A multi-policy discount of 12 percent applies when you also insure a vehicle with Acme. A protective device discount of 5 percent applies when the home has a centrally monitored burglar or fire alarm. A claims-free discount of 8 percent applies when you have had no claims in the last 3 years. A new roof discount of 4 percent applies when the roof is less than 10 years old.

Kova Bank Account FAQ
Sample document. Kova Bank is a fictional bank created for this demonstration. Nothing in this document describes a real bank account.

How do I open an account?
You can open a Kova account in the Kova mobile app or at kova.example in about ten minutes. You must be at least 18 years old and have a valid government-issued photo ID and a residential address. The minimum opening deposit is 25 dollars for Everyday Checking and 100 dollars for High Yield Savings. Joint accounts can be opened with up to two owners.
section: How do I open an account?

text:
Is there a monthly fee on Everyday Checking?
Everyday Checking has a monthly maintenance fee of 8 dollars. The fee is waived for any statement cycle in which you keep a daily balance of at least 1,500 dollars or receive at least 500 dollars in direct deposits. The fee is also waived for students under 25 years old.
section: Is there a monthly fee on Everyday Checking?

text:
What happens if I spend more than my balance?
Kova does not charge overdraft fees on Everyday Checking. If a debit card purchase or ATM withdrawal would overdraw your account, it is declined. You can turn on free Overdraft Transfer, which moves money from your linked Kova savings account to cover a transaction.
section: What happens if I spend more than my balance?

text:
How much interest does High Yield Savings earn?
High Yield Savings currently earns 3.80 percent APY. The rate is variable and may change at any time. Interest is compounded daily and credited to your account monthly. You can make 6 free withdrawals or transfers out of savings per statement cycle, and each additional withdrawal costs 5 dollars.
section: How much interest does High Yield Savings earn?

text:
How long do transfers and wires take?
Standard ACH transfers to other banks arrive in 1 to 3 business days. Transfers to other Kova customers are instant and free. Outgoing domestic wires cost 25 dollars and outgoing international wires cost 45 dollars. Incoming wires are free. Wires requested before 3 p.m. Eastern time on a business day are sent the same day.
section: How long do transfers and wires take?

text:
What are the mobile check deposit limits?
You can deposit up to 5,000 dollars per day and up to 10,000 dollars in any 30-day period with mobile check deposit. The first 225 dollars of a mobile deposit is available on the next business day, and the rest is usually available within 2 business days. Keep the paper check for 14 days after the deposit, then destroy it.
section: What are the mobile check deposit limits?

text:
What should I do if my card is lost or stolen?
Freeze your card right away in the Kova app, then report it as lost or stolen in the app or by calling the number on the back of the card. A replacement card arrives in 5 to 7 business days, and expedited delivery in 2 business days is free. If you report an unauthorized debit card transaction within 2 business days, you are not responsible for it under the Kova zero liability promise.
section: What should I do if my card is lost or stolen?

text:
How do I close my account?
You can close an account at any time in the app or by calling Kova. There is no fee to close an account, except that accounts closed within 90 days of opening are charged a 25 dollar early closure fee. Any remaining balance is sent to you by transfer or by mailed check.
section: How do I close my account?

text:
How can I contact Kova?
Kova customer support is available by phone every day from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. Eastern time, and by chat in the app 24 hours a day. The fictional support number for this sample is 1-800-555-0199.

KOVA BANK PRIVACY NOTICE
Sample document. Kova Bank is a fictional bank created for this demonstration.

WHAT INFORMATION KOVA COLLECTS
Kova collects the information you give when you open an account, such as your name, address, date of birth, government ID number and income. Kova also collects information about your transactions, your account balances, and the device and location data the Kova app uses to detect fraud.

HOW KOVA SHARES INFORMATION
Kova shares personal information with service providers that process payments and print statements, with credit bureaus, and with government agencies when the law requires it. Kova does not sell personal information. Kova shares information with partner companies for their marketing only if you agree, and you can withdraw that agreement at any time.

YOUR CHOICES
You can limit sharing for marketing by changing the privacy settings in the Kova app or by calling customer support. Your choice takes effect within 30 days and stays in place until you change it. If you have a joint account, a choice made by one account owner applies to both owners.

HOW LONG KOVA KEEPS INFORMATION
Kova keeps account records for 7 years after an account is closed, because banking regulations require it. After that period the records are deleted or anonymized.

YOUR RIGHTS
You can ask Kova for a copy of the personal information it holds about you, or ask Kova to correct it. Kova responds to these requests within 30 days. Requests can be made in the app under Settings, Privacy.

Kova Rewards Visa Card: Pricing and Terms
Sample document. Kova Bank is a fictional bank created for this demonstration. Nothing in this document describes a real credit card.
section: Kova Rewards Visa Card: Pricing and Terms

text:
Card Overview and Rewards
The Kova Rewards Visa card earns 1.5 percent cash back on all eligible purchases. Grocery store purchases earn 3 percent cash back on up to 6,000 dollars of grocery spending each calendar year, after which they earn 1.5 percent. There is no annual fee for the Kova Rewards Visa card. Cash back can be redeemed as a statement credit or a deposit into a Kova checking or savings account. The minimum redemption is 25 dollars. Rewards do not expire while the account is open and in good standing, but unredeemed rewards are forfeited if the account is closed because of fraud or abuse.

Interest Rates
The purchase APR is a variable rate between 19.99 percent and 27.99 percent, based on your creditworthiness. New cardholders receive an introductory APR of 0 percent on purchases for the first 15 months after account opening. Balance transfers made within 60 days of account opening receive an introductory APR of 0 percent for 12 months. After the introductory period, the purchase APR applies to any remaining transferred balance. The cash advance APR is 29.49 percent, variable. Kova does not charge a penalty APR.

Fees
The balance transfer fee is 3 percent of each transfer, with a minimum of 5 dollars. The cash advance fee is 5 percent of each advance, with a minimum of 10 dollars. There is no foreign transaction fee. The late payment fee is up to 30 dollars for the first late payment and up to 41 dollars if another payment is late within the next six billing cycles. The returned payment fee is up to 25 dollars. Kova does not charge an over-the-limit fee.

Payments and Grace Period
Your due date is at least 25 days after the close of each billing cycle. Kova will not charge interest on purchases if you pay your entire balance by the due date each month. This interest-free period is called the grace period. The minimum payment is the greater of 35 dollars or 1 percent of the new balance plus interest and fees, or the full balance if it is less than 35 dollars. You can set up automatic payments for the minimum payment, the statement balance, or a fixed amount in the Kova mobile app.
